beats.story: We're all piled into the big boardroom on the fifth floor, and we've sat here long enough that the sharp cologne Jean Adler's been dabbing into his neck since, like, 1984 has all but disappeared. All the beady freaking eyes face forward; this room feels more like a stadium. I twist the metal water bottle sitting on my lap in my clammy hands and try to steady my breath. Cliff is sitting at the end of the largest table next to mine. He's got his notepad out, and the way his pen is moving, I'd bet big money that he's doodling. But when I tried to squint and see earlier, he caught me peeking and smiled. Armin had his HR meeting earlier today. When he returned, he DMed me: Went well for you.
beats.story_cn: 我们全被塞进五楼的大会议室，坐得够久了，让·阿德勒从1984年起就往脖颈上猛喷的刺鼻古龙水味儿几乎散尽了。一双双贼溜溜的狗眼全盯着前方；这房间简直像个体育场。我把腿上的金属水瓶在汗湿的手心里来回拧着，试图稳住呼吸。克利夫坐在最大那张桌子的另一头，就在我旁边。他摊开笔记本，看那支笔划动的样子，我敢押重注说他肯定在涂鸦。但刚才我眯眼偷瞄时被他逮个正着，这小子居然冲我笑了。阿明今天早些时候去开了人力资源会。回来后他私信我：你这边挺顺利。

beats.story: Didn't tell him about my mom. And as relieved as I was that he vouched for me, it hit even harder that he confided that. Gregory is standing at the front of the room, listing off a new policy that has already been emailed company-wide several times. Rhonda nods, smiling way too hard. She's propped herself front and center at the table to take meeting minutes that nobody asked for. She'll likely file them away in some cabinet afterward, never to be seen again. My mind feels like it's literally shaking in my skull. All the words I'm going to try to say replay over each other in discordant nonsense.
beats.story_cn: 没告诉她我妈的事。虽然庆幸他为我作证，但想到他竟对我吐露心事，这冲击反而更甚。格雷戈里站在房间前方，重申那封全公司已转发数遍的新政策。罗达拼命点头微笑，她抢坐到会议桌最前排正中位置做没人要求的会议记录。八成事后就被她塞进某个文件柜，再无见天之日。我感觉脑子在颅骨里震颤不止，所有准备要说的话混乱交叠成一片无意义的噪音。

beats.story: I wish I could see Cliff's cat sketches from here. Gregory claps his hands once as he shifts topics. It seems like he's close to wrapping up. "Before we go, it's time for the ideas and opinions session. I myself have been brainstorming an exciting incentive program" -- he pauses to raise his brows enticingly -- "But I'd love to hear any thoughts you've all been tinkering with first." All the expressions remain neutral and uninspired by this, except for Caitlin, who nods way too hard. We start with two suggestions from supply chain people that have already been suggested a dozen times before. With each passing comment, every tick of the clock, my skin tightens and cools. I look around the table and try to decipher if anyone will be sympathetic should I faint in the middle of the room when my brain snaps from nerves.
beats.story_cn: 真希望从这儿能看到克利夫画的猫漫画。格雷戈里拍了下手切换话题，看起来快收尾了。“散会前，咱们进入创意提案环节。我个人琢磨了个超带劲的激励计划”——他故意挑起眉毛顿了顿——“不过很乐意先听听各位最近在捣鼓的点子。”除了凯特琳夸张猛点头，其他人脸上都挂着副漠不关心的扑克脸。先是供应链同事提了两条已经被说过八百遍的建议。每过一句发言，每一声秒针滴答，我的肌肤就阵阵绷紧发凉。环视长桌琢磨着，要是我脑子被紧张扯断、当场晕厥，不知谁会发发善心。

beats.story: Larry stands, shiny sheen on his forehead, armpits darkened and heavy from perspiration. "Good god," comes from some unknown voice in the back. My breath halts in involuntary sympathy as he clears his throat. "I think we should implement some type of town hall meeting every now and then to really form a cohesive office." He stares at Gregory, an intense smile pointed toward him like an attack. "We could share ideas and go over some of the bigger elements that affect multiple departments." Did he just suggest the very thing we're doing? My eyes draw to Cliff, who is wincing and nodding along. He writes something down, lips pressed together. Larry grins like he really said something there and lingers while a tumbleweed passes.
beats.story_cn: 拉里站起身，额头泛着油光，腋下的汗渍又深又重。“老天，”后排传来某个不明声音。他清了清嗓子，我不由自主地屏住了呼吸，感同身受。“我认为我们应该定期举行某种形式的全员大会，以真正凝聚团队。”他盯着格雷戈里，那抹灿烂的笑容像柄匕首直直指向对方。“我们可以交流想法，讨论一些涉及多个部门的重大议题。”他该不会刚刚提议的正是我们此刻正在做的事？我的目光转向克里夫，他正龇牙咧嘴地点头附和。他写下些什么，嘴唇紧抿。拉里咧嘴笑着，仿佛真说了句绝妙的话，在原地徘徊时恰有一株风滚草悄然滚过。

beats.story: Finally, Greg mutters, "Thank you." Larry retreats to his seat. Taking advantage of the opening, Caitlin juts out her chin. "I was thinking we could sort information going to other departments into categories to better streamline." She stands up and begins passing around photocopied pages of her plan. "I've got a list of areas this would optimize and prevent lost communication." A few people in marketing nod enthusiastically. Gregory looks at her document and does his version of a smile. It's an unfortunate win for her. She raises her eyebrows toward Garret in silent celebration. But Joy mutters, "What about the chain to invoicing?" "Ah yes, well, I've designed a -- " Her phone dings and she pulls it from her back pocket, tapping it.
beats.story_cn: 最后，格雷戈里咕哝道：“谢谢。”拉里退回座位。凯特琳趁势扬起下巴。“我在想，我们可以把发往其他部门的信息分门别类，以提升效率。”她站起身，开始分发她计划的影印页。“这里列出了能优化并避免沟通遗漏的几个环节。”市场部几个人热情地点头。格雷戈里看着她的文件，露出了他招牌式的微笑。对她而言，这是一场惨胜。她朝加雷特挑起眉毛，无声地庆祝。但乔伊低声道：“那发票流程呢？”“啊，对，这个，我设计了一个——”她的手机叮咚一响，她从后裤袋掏出手机飞速点按。

I divert from her gaze, and she blinks several times. "That's something I'm working to incorporate as well. Thanks." Her voice is meek, her entire aura suddenly smaller as she makes her way back to her mesh boardroom seat.
beats.story_cn: “抱歉，忘静音了。”她眉头蹙起。“我刚说到哪了？我是说我已经制定了一个……”她的目光扫过桌面，最终落在我身上。我避开她的视线，她眨了好几下眼睛。“这也是我正努力纳入考量的部分。谢谢。”她的声音很轻，整个人气场骤然收缩，悄无声息地挪回网面办公椅。

beats.story: My hand raises, shaky and sweating. Gregory's expression shifts to almost a scowl, almost offended. "Miss Smith, do you have something?" Every single face in the room turns toward me. My stomach flips as I stand. My legs have morphed into Jell-O. I open my mouth, but all the words in the world seem to mesh on my tongue and I'm sure I'll say something offensive instead, because my brain likes to fuck me up like that. I clear my throat, but my voice is still pitchy as I say, "I noticed several departments keep important data in silos, like supply chain and accounting regarding seasonal sales." All the faces remain deadpan, their eyes glassy and lifeless. The only sound in the room comes from Larry Goodwin chugging his water bottle.
beats.story_cn: 我的手颤抖着举起，手心沁满汗水。格雷戈里的神情转为近乎蹙眉，仿佛受到冒犯。"史密斯小姐，有要补充的？"房间里每张脸都转向我。起身时胃部紧缩，双腿已软如果冻。我张开嘴，千言万语却在舌尖凝成乱麻——我确信自己会说出冒犯的话，因为我的大脑总爱这样捉弄人。清了清喉咙，声音仍发紧："我注意到多个部门各自保存关键数据，比如供应链与会计部门对季节性销售的记录就相互割裂。"众人依旧面无表情，眼神空洞呆滞。唯剩拉里·古德温咕咚咕咚喝水的声音在房间回荡。

My eyes shift to Rhonda, who is pursing her lips. Then to Armin, who raises his eyebrows. I look toward Cliff. He puts his pen down and nods at me encouragingly. beats.story: For reasons I don't understand, the words I write are: Streamline Business Jean: nailed it The meeting draws to a close, and as people shuffle out of their seats they shoot me grins and nods and call out short affirmations like "nice job." A lightness takes over. I want to see Cliff smile at me again, but he's too busy talking with Gregory and Larry in the corner. The poor guy. Caitlin marches in front of me with dropped shoulders as she stabs her phone. She frowns, red-faced, like she might burst. I take a breath. I can relax now. I spend the lunch hour walking to the mall, something I've done countless times before, only this time isn't as isolated or dire as my usual ganders.
beats.story_cn: 也不知怎的，我写下的字句是：精简业务流程·琼：完美收官。会议临近尾声，人们挪动椅子起身离座，朝我投来笑容与点头，嘴里蹦出简短的肯定词，比如“干得漂亮”。一股轻松感弥漫开来。我想再看克里夫对我展颜，可他正忙着在角落和格雷戈里、拉里交谈。这可怜家伙。凯特琳耷拉着肩膀冲到我面前，手指猛戳手机屏幕。她眉头紧锁，满脸涨红，仿佛随时要爆发。我深吸一口气。现在可以放松了。午休时间我走去商场，这已是我无数次走过的路，只是这一次的游荡，不再像往常那般孤立无援、凄惶绝望。

beats.story: People always want to see what you bought and then have you show it off with a song and dance for our capitalist lords. When I return, the afternoon office is mostly silent, apart from the hum of the health hazard of a fan on Jean's desk that's smudged grey with caked- on dust and human debris after years of slowly dying in this place. Water leaks from the cooler in torturously unpredictable drips, yet nobody is willing to simply stop it, myself included. Only Caitlin isn't taking this time of rest seriously. She's been zombie- focused on her screen since the meeting, frantically pulling out folders and notebooks and clicking her mouse faster and more often than usual. As she marches toward the copy room with a document in hand, I dare a peep her way. Her jaw is set and her eyes look tired. Rhonda marches around to my cubicle as soon as Caitlin's out of sight.
beats.story_cn: 人们总想瞧瞧你买了什么，然后让你唱念做打地炫耀一番，好给资本家老爷们助兴。我返回时，午后的办公室一片死寂，唯独琼桌上那台积满灰尘与经年累积的人体碎屑、已病入膏肓的风扇发出嗡嗡的噪音，还有饮水机渗漏着折磨人心的、毫无规律的滴水声，却无人——包括我在内——愿伸手关掉它。唯有凯特琳对这段休憩时光不屑一顾。会议结束后她便如僵尸般死死盯着屏幕，疯狂翻找文件夹和笔记本，鼠标点击得比往常更快更密。当她手持文件朝复印室疾步走去时，我斗胆偷瞥了一眼。她牙关紧咬，眼神疲惫。凯特琳身影刚消失，罗达便杀到了我的隔间。

beats.story: "Can I come in?" she whispers. I nod, and she sidles even closer than her visit here last week. "So, as you know, Caitlin's engaged." "Yes." I force myself to smile as brightly as Sir Sunny D, even as dread spins up my spine. I know exactly where this is going. "So, us Morale Boosters should plan a surprise engagement party on Friday, when she normally goes for drinks. Just a small one with us friends at work and the happy couple." I don't mean for my expression to shift -- I really try -- but Rhonda's eyes droop a bit as she notices my reaction. "It'll be small," she continues. "Nothing to outshine Gregory's work anniversary in two weeks.
beats.story_cn: “我能进来吗？”她轻声问道。我点点头，她挨得比上周来时更近。“那个，你也知道，凯特琳订婚了。”“嗯。”我强迫自己笑得像阳光先生般灿烂，任由不祥的预感顺着脊椎爬升。我完全知道这场谈话要导向何处。“所以我们士气鼓舞者应该计划个惊喜订婚派对，就定在周五——她照例去喝酒的日子。规模不大，就公司里这些朋友和那对幸福的情侣。”我没想变脸——我真的尽力了——但朗达注意到我的表情时眼帘微微垂落。“会很简朴，”她继续道，“绝不会抢了两周后格雷戈里工作周年庆的风头。”

beats.story: You won't have to do much, but could you help me on the day of with decorations? Your first assignment?" FFS. At face value, it's such a small ask, decorations. Only the idea of going to a party to celebrate Caitlin may make me break out in hives. But if I say no, it'll mean Rhonda has to do everything alone, yet again. I nod and force out, "Happy to." Her whole face brightens. "Thank you, dear. We now have two parties to plan -- so fun!" She lowers her voice as Caitlin rounds the corner.
beats.story_cn: “你不用做太多，但当天能帮我布置会场吗？你的首个任务？”老天。表面看只是布置会场这般小事，可光是想到要去参加庆祝凯特琳的派对就足以让我起一身鸡皮疙瘩。但若拒绝，又意味着朗达得再次独自承担一切。我点点头挤出一句：“乐意效劳。”她整张脸都亮了起来。“谢谢亲爱的。现在我们得筹备两场派对了——多有意思！”她压低声音，因为凯特琳正转过墙角走来。

beats.story: "I'll go make a call in the boardroom to book the table." My mouth twitches; I can't help the smile as Rhonda marches off. Because her steps are bouncier. Caitlin squeaks back into her chair, and I sneak another glance her way. She's typing rapidly, yet the bags under her eyes rest heavy like flags of defeat. Caitlin deserves a party before I beat her out for this job, at the very least.
beats.story_cn: “我去会议室打电话订位。”罗恩达大步流星地离去，我的嘴角忍不住抽了抽——看她脚步蹦跳得更欢快了。凯特琳哧溜缩回椅子里，我又偷瞄了她一眼。她手指在键盘上飞舞，可眼下的乌青沉重得像两面战败的旗帜。至少在我挤掉她得到这份工作前，她值得办场庆祝派对。
